transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because flying has gotten… really frightening for me. Just the thought of getting on an airplane scares me so badly. I know logically it doesn’t make sense, but my body reacts like that plane is going to fall.
Is it just flying that scares you, or are there other situations that cause you similar fear?
It’s really just flying. The thought of getting on an airplane is what sets it off. I know in my head it doesn’t make sense, but I get this strong fear like the plane is going to fall.
Does anything else trigger this kind of fear for you, or is it only when you think about or are in situations involving flying?
It’s only flying. Even just thinking about getting on an airplane can set it off. I know it doesn’t make sense, but my body reacts like that plane is going to fall.
How long have you been experiencing this fear of flying?
About seven months now. It started after I had a really turbulent flight on a small plane, right after I’d lost my clinic job. Since then, the fear’s just stayed with me.
Has your fear of flying stopped you from doing things you want or need to do?

Yes. I’ve turned down coverage work that would require flying, and that’s cost me money. It’s also made some colleagues question if they can count on me. I’ve missed important professional meetings too, and I’ve put off visiting my family because I’d have to fly.
Have you been avoiding other modes of transportation or situations because of your fear, aside from flying?

Not really other transportation, no. It’s the flying part and getting to the airport. I’ve canceled clinic coverage, skipped medical meetings, and put off seeing my family in Honduras because I just can’t make myself go unless I’m shaking and holding on to someone the whole time.
Have you ever had a panic attack while on an airplane?

I haven’t had one on a plane recently because I’ve been avoiding flying, but even just getting an email about a rural shift that would mean taking a flight sets me off right away. My heart starts pounding, my hands get sweaty, and I feel like I can’t breathe until I close the message.
Have you experienced any panic attacks in situations other than when thinking about or preparing to fly?
I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed that happening outside of flying or things that make me think I might have to fly.
Has your fear of flying affected your relationships with family or friends?

Yes. I’ve put off seeing my family because I can’t get myself on a plane, and that’s been hard. With friends and colleagues, too—I’ve turned down coverage that requires flying, and it’s cost me income. I think some people at work are starting to wonder if they can count on me. I’ve also missed important meetings because of it.
Do you experience excessive worry about things other than flying?
Not really. I mean, I worry about normal work and family stuff like anyone, but it doesn’t feel excessive or out of control the way the flying issue does.
How would you describe the level of distress you feel when you think about flying?
It’s severe. Just thinking about getting on a plane scares me so much, and I know in my head it doesn’t really make sense, but my body reacts like the plane is going to fall.
